blocks.text: The Department of Arrivals
Middle Era One · Satirical chamber play · Three acts
Persons and place
ILEX, a station translator whose position has been renamed Passenger Clarity Associate.
VARO, registrar of arrivals, responsible for a recent improvement in the figures.
NACRE, a visiting gardener in a low, many-footed traveling body.
THE ANNOUNCEMENT, an automatic station system. It has no character development.

A bright hall in the Pale Concordance Station. Three identical arrows point in different directions. A single irregular bench survives near a closed departure gate. The bench has a hollow beneath it, a ledge beside it, and surfaces at four heights.
Act I. An excellent year
THE ANNOUNCEMENT: Welcome. You have arrived.
NACRE: I haven't.
THE ANNOUNCEMENT: Thank you for arriving.
ILEX: It doesn't listen after the first sentence.
NACRE: Then why does it have a second?
ILEX: Hospitality.
[Nacre sets down a covered bowl. Something beneath its cloth moves in a slow circular pattern.]
NACRE: I need the low-water gate.
ILEX: Which low-water gate?
NACRE: The one that admits visitors after the roots have closed, before the upper gardens wake, while the carriers are still receiving.
ILEX: I remember that route. It used to have a long name.
NACRE: It still has a long name.
ILEX: On our boards it is now Garden.
NACRE: Which garden?
ILEX: There are seven objections filed on that subject.
[Varo enters carrying a transparent display.]
VARO: Eighty-three percent fewer translation delays.
ILEX: Good morning.
VARO: It is. We are entitled to say so numerically.
NACRE: Where is the low-water gate?
VARO: You are already at your destination.
NACRE: No, I am at your station.
VARO: Under the new accounting system, arriving at a destination-capable facility constitutes successful arrival.
NACRE: What constitutes successful departure?
VARO: We are not the Department of Departures.
[The bowl moves. Ilex looks toward it.]
NACRE: These must be home before their quiet phase ends.
VARO: Plants?
NACRE: Root guests. They are traveling to a compatible bed.
VARO: Biological cargo?
NACRE: They may refuse the bed. I cannot declare them cargo simply to hurry them through your hall.
ILEX: They need a damp transit surface, a pressure adjustment, and a receiving signal. We used to keep the instructions with the destination name.
VARO: We still keep them.
ILEX: In the history archive.
VARO: Therefore preserved.
NACRE: Can your history archive open the gate?
VARO: Its visitor figures are excellent.
Act II. A minor inconvenience
[Later. The covered bowl rests in the bench's hollow. Ilex has darkened that part of the hall. Varo has restored the lights twice.]
VARO: People must be able to see where they are going.
NACRE: These people are trying to remain asleep.
VARO: They do not appear on the passenger declaration.
NACRE: Your declaration asked for the number of bodies.
VARO: Yes.
NACRE: That number changes during travel. I wrote “please ask.”
VARO: The system read that as three.
ILEX: Why three?
VARO: Three words.
[A pause.]
ILEX: “Please ask” is two words.
VARO: There was a note.
NACRE: The note was “urgent.”
VARO: There we are.
[Ilex turns off the light above the bowl. Varo does not turn it on again.]
ILEX: I can retrieve the old passage record. I'll need a temporary increase in translation allowance.
VARO: Every extra channel reinstates a delay.
ILEX: Every missing channel reinstates this conversation.

VARO: There were real problems with the old system. Visitors were humiliated for not knowing local forms. Some waited entire cycles for a translator. A person with a damaged register could be refused passage over a distinction they could not physically make.
ILEX: I know. I was one of the translators they waited for.
VARO: Then you know what the standard signs accomplished.
ILEX: They got people to this hall. We have confused that with getting them through it.
[Varo sits on the high end of the bench. It is too narrow for the form they use. They move to the lower surface.]
VARO: My first journey took nine cycles to arrange. The receiving world treated my arrival as a favor. I wanted nobody to experience that again.
NACRE: I believe you.
VARO: Thank you.
NACRE: Open the archive.
[Varo does. The wall displays a dense field of old instructions. Ilex studies it. Nacre lifts the bowl's cloth, checks the root guests, then covers them again.]
ILEX: This record is obsolete.
VARO: We were assured it was complete.
ILEX: Complete when collected. The receiving root bed has changed twice since this sequence. Its invitation would now arrive as a drainage request.
NACRE: Yes. That was a difficult season.
VARO: Can you repair the sequence?
ILEX: Not alone. Nacre knows the current bed. I can retain the distinctions through the station. Somebody at the far gate must answer for the receiving side.
VARO: The automated receiver accepts the standard phrase.
NACRE: The standard phrase says my guests consent to being planted.
VARO: It says they are ready to arrive.
NACRE: You have merged those meanings.
[The movement under the cloth quickens.]
NACRE: We have less time now.
Act III. An arrival that takes longer
[The main departure gate lights. It is white, even, and perfectly clear.]
THE ANNOUNCEMENT: Your route is ready. Please proceed.
VARO: It found a compatible destination.
ILEX: It found the nearest standard garden.
NACRE: That garden keeps its beds dry through the receiving phase. My guests would wake before they could hold.
THE ANNOUNCEMENT: Your route is ready. Please proceed.
[Nacre lifts the bowl away from the gate.]
VARO: The successful-arrival field is already complete.
ILEX: Change it.
VARO: There is no field for arrived here, not yet arrived there.
ILEX: There is a notes field.
VARO: Notes are not included in the report.
NACRE: I am beginning to understand your excellent year.
[Varo closes the display. The hall becomes quieter without its soft confirmation tones.]
VARO: What do you need me to authorize?
ILEX: A local hold on the automatic gate. A live receiving exchange. Enough channel time to establish whether passage is welcome. And a record that it might not be.
VARO: The last condition will register as failure.
NACRE: If the bed cannot receive them, I want to know before I enter.
[Varo places the automatic gate on hold. The announcement begins its first sentence and stops after “Your.”]
ILEX: We can do this in parts. I will describe the host conditions as Nacre gives them. The receiving keeper can correct them. We will preserve the corrections, not merely the final phrase.
VARO: Shall I mark Nacre as the responsible speaker?
NACRE: For the conditions I know. The guests answer for themselves when they wake.

[Ilex begins. Their speech opens several tonal relationships at once. This performance does not reproduce the utterance: the actors may represent the work with light, pauses, and a changing line across the floor. The line advances only when an answer comes from the far side.]
[The first answer is refusal.]
NACRE: That bed has closed.
VARO: Then the journey is lost?
NACRE: There is another. I need to ask whether its carriers have finished.
[They ask. The second answer contains a correction, an offer, and a condition Ilex cannot immediately hold. The line breaks.]
ILEX: Again, please.
[The answer repeats more slowly. Varo finds the bench's removable damp tray and places it beneath the bowl. Nacre acknowledges this without interrupting the exchange.]
[At last a narrow gate opens beside the bright one. It contains a low passage, dim moisture, and the faint motion of a living receiving bed.]
THE ANNOUNCEMENT: Your route is—
VARO: Quiet.
[Varo disconnects the announcement.]
NACRE: I will take them to the threshold. Some may choose to stay in the bowl. If they do, I will need a return route.
ILEX: It will remain open through this receiving interval.
VARO: I will stay until you answer.
[Nacre enters. The gate remains. Ilex sits beside Varo, exhausted.]
VARO: I have made our figures worse.
ILEX: By how much?
VARO: I do not yet know how to count it.
[A reply comes from the gate. Most of the root guests have accepted the bed. Two remain with Nacre. They will come back through the station.]
VARO: Two passengers returning.
ILEX: Ask.
[Varo opens the exchange.]
Coda. The complaint
[Several cycles later. A new sign stands beneath the three identical arrows. It reads: IF THESE DIRECTIONS ARE INSUFFICIENT, ASK HERE. Under that, in another hand: YOU MAY ALSO POINT.]
[Varo is taking a complicated complaint from a traveler outside the scene. Ilex tends the bench's damp tray.]
VARO: Yes, the delay is real. No, we are not charging you for explaining it. Yes, I will record the distinction.
[They listen.]
VARO: No. I cannot promise the entire network will change.
[They listen longer.]
VARO: This desk is still open.

[A maintenance report arrives. The local exception has been classified as an avoidable inefficiency. Ilex places it beside the complaint rather than concealing it. The larger station remains pale; most gates still use the old standard.]
[Nacre returns with an empty bowl and something wrapped in damp cloth.]
NACRE: They sent a cutting. It may accept your tray.
VARO: How long will we have to wait?
NACRE: Ask it when it wakes.
[Varo makes space on the bench.]
Curtain.

outline.title: Act III. An arrival that takes longer
